approach: Reference design for XML Book Library: begin with synthetic data and a written contract, then create the smallest valid document/schema/stylesheet needed for the required features. Add tests for valid, malformed and boundary input. Represent a reading library as structured XML and verify well-formedness and simple constraints.
key_decisions: Keep source documents and expected outputs in version control.
Validate output using the exact schema/processor intended for deployment.
Block unnecessary external-resource resolution and bound document size/depth.
Record namespace, encoding, processor version, compatibility, and known limitations.
acceptance_criteria: Title, author, genre and publication year elements
Well-formedness checks and sample invalid cases
explanation: This is a reference design rather than a claim that the project was deployed or run. Equivalent solutions are acceptable if they satisfy the acceptance criteria and provide evidence for expected behavior.
